results: 1. Complete physical examination with focused localization of the pain, including inspection, palpation, range-of-motion, neurologic, and vascular assessment
cranial nerve examination: bilateral post-paralytic facial synkinesis; narrowed left palpebral fissure
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
synkinesis assessment (eye closure with platysma/frontalis): co-contraction of eye closure with the left platysma and left frontalis; right lower-lip curling on speech and mastication
palpebral fissure width both sides: narrowed LEFT palpebral fissure from established synkinesis
ear and mastoid examination: normal, no vesicles
parotid and neck palpation: no mass
voice and hoarseness assessment: normal voice
gait, ability to run, and limb sensation: normal
full blood count and ESR/CRP: normal
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
4. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
full blood count and ESR/CRP: normal

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acquired post-paralytic facial synkinesis due to remote facial nerve palsy, most consistent with sequelae of bilateral idiopathic Bell’s palsy

Alternative 1: Facial synkinesis following prior traumatic, surgical, or other acquired facial nerve injury

Alternative 2: Hemifacial spasm

Alternative 3: Congenital facial nerve miswiring (congenital facial synkinesis)
